description: Filers: the address of the filer, as the agency records it, in Japanese.

Facts: whether the figure is consolidated or of the filer alone, as the conversion labels it ('連結', '個別', 'その他'). The context identifier carries the same thing as a dimension member and is the more reliable of the two, so both are kept.
Filers: the stated capital of the filer in millions of yen, carried as the agency publishes it rather than parsed; empty for a filer that states none.

Issues: the day the run that wrote the row was made. The issues of a partition are replaced as a whole when it is checked again, so this says when the rows that are there were found rather than when the problem arose.

Facts: the element the fact reports, as the conversion writes it, prefix and name (jppfs_cor:Assets, jpcrp_cor:NetSales). Four prefixes are the taxonomy -- jppfs_cor the financial statements, jpcrp_cor the disclosure ordinance, jpdei_cor the document and entity information, jpigp_cor the IFRS edition -- and a prefix built from the form and the filer's own EDINET code, as in jpcrp030000-asr_E03270-000, marks a concept the filer created for its own report.
Filers: whether the filer reports on a consolidated basis, as the agency records it ('有' yes, '無' no).

Facts: the context identifier of the fact, as the conversion writes it, for instance CurrentYearDuration or Prior1YearInstant_NonConsolidatedMember. It names the period relative to the filing's own and then the dimensions, and it is carried verbatim because PRDSTART and PRDEND are resolved from it rather than reported.
Filings: the description of the document shown in the search results of the disclosure site, which names the kind of report and the period in Japanese.

Facts: the dimensions of the fact, as the part of the context identifier that follows the period, for instance NonConsolidatedMember or OrdinaryShareMember. A report may break a figure down by a member it created itself, including one per director.
Filings: whether an official of a finance bureau has withheld the document from disclosure. Carried as published and acted on nowhere: a filing is not dropped for it.

Facts: which document of the filing the fact came from, by the form that names the file in the archive: jpcrp030000-asr for an annual securities report, jpaud-aai-cn for the audit report the agency converts beside it.

Filings: the kind of document, as the agency codes it (120 annual securities report, 130 its correction, 140 quarterly, 160 semi-annual). fincommons.financialreport.edinet.common.REPORT_TYPES names the ones that carry statements.

The EDINET code of the filer, a letter E and five digits, which is the key the tables of this module are organised by. It is not the securities code and not the corporate number; all three are carried and none is derived from another.
Filings: whether an official of a finance bureau has corrected the information held about the document. Carried as published.

Facts: the identifier of a fact. The conversion gives one none, so it is made from the filing, the document of it, the element, the context and an occurrence number. The number is needed because the element and the context do not identify a fact: a figure is often tagged in several places in one report.

Filings: the year the filing was submitted, which the table is partitioned by. The year a filing was made only moves forward; the period it reports on does not, a filer that changes its year end reporting two or none.
The document management number (書類管理番号) the API addresses a filing by, for instance S100VWVY. It identifies a document within EDINET and is the key a filing is collected and read by.
Filings: the form code of the document, which with the ordinance code says which prescribed form it was filed on.
Filings: the fund code, where the document is filed for an investment fund rather than for the filer as a whole; empty for an operating company's report.

Filings: whether the agency converted the filing's XBRL to CSV ('1' yes). It is the column that decides whether a filing can contribute figures at all, the counterpart of a null JSONURL in the esef module.
Filings: whether the filer lodged an English version of the document ('1' yes). It is a document in its own right and not a translation of the Japanese one.
Filings: whether the document carries XBRL ('1' yes). The CSV conversion is made from it, so a filing without XBRL has no CSV either.
Filings: the calendar day whose index named the filing. The index API answers for one day at a time, so this is the unit a run collects by and what says which index a row came from.
Filers: the industry of the filer, in the agency's own classification, in Japanese.

Issues: the code of the data quality check the record failed, one row per check it failed. fincommons.dataquality.describe_check turns it into the sentence that says what the code means, how severe it is and what to do about it. A record nothing objected to has no row in the table at all.

The corporate number (法人番号) of the National Tax Agency, thirteen digits, which every Japanese legal person has. It is the identifier of these tables most likely to be shared with a register outside EDINET; whether it reaches the legal entity identifier the esef tables are keyed by is a question for the data and nothing here derives one from the other.
Filers: the kind of filer, as the agency classifies it (a domestic legal person or partnership, a foreign company, an individual), in Japanese.

Facts: the Japanese name of the element, which the conversion states beside it. Neither of the other two regimes carries a label, the ESEF labels living in a taxonomy this package does not read and the Commission publishing none, so it is the only thing in these tables that says what a concept means to a reader who does not know the taxonomy.

Filings: whether the document is on public view ('1'), within the administrative extension period ('2'), or past both ('0'). A filing in the last state is still named by an index collected earlier and can no longer be fetched, which is why the Bronze layer of this module is the only lasting copy of what it holds.
Filers: whether the filer is listed, as the agency records it ('上場' listed, '非上場' not).
The name of the filer, as the agency records it, in Japanese.
Filers: the name of the filer in Latin script, as the agency records it.
Filers: the reading of the filer's name in katakana, which is how the agency's own search orders them.
Filings: the ordinance code of the document, which with the form code says which prescribed form it was filed on.
Filings: the document management number of the document this one belongs to, where it is part of another; empty for a document that stands alone.
Filings: the last day of the period the document reports on, which for a securities report is its financial year and for a quarterly report its quarter.
Filings: the first day of the period the document reports on; empty for a document that reports on an instant or on no period.

Facts: the last day of the period the fact is about, or the day an instant stands for. It is resolved and not reported: for the current year and the comparative it is the date the filing states for itself in its document and entity information, and for anything further back it is that date shifted by whole years, which is exact only where the filer's years are of equal length. Empty where the context names a period this module does not resolve.
Facts: the first day of the period the fact is about; empty for a fact reported at an instant, which is how the two are told apart. Resolved rather than reported, as PRDEND is.

Facts: which period the fact is about, relative to the filing, in the agency's own words ('当期', '前期', '前々期', '提出日時点'). It says the same as the period part of the context identifier and is kept so that what PRDSTART and PRDEND were resolved from can be read without parsing a context.
The securities code of a listed filer: the four-digit ticker with a check digit appended, so 13760 is ticker 1376. Empty for a filer that is not listed.
Facts: whether the element is a flow over a period or a balance at a moment, as the conversion labels it ('期間' a period, '時点' an instant).
Filings: when the document was submitted to EDINET, as the agency states it.

Facts: the value of a fact that is not a number, as the conversion writes it. It also holds the full-width dash the conversion writes where a figure does not apply, which is a statement about the figure and is kept rather than dropped.

Facts: the unit of the fact as the conversion names it (JPY, shares, pure, JPYPerShares, tCO2e); empty where the element has none. The conversion also states a label for it in Japanese, which is not carried.

Facts: the value of a numeric fact, as reported, in UNIT and without any scaling. Empty where the fact has no number, which includes a fact that carries a unit and a full-width dash for its value because the figure does not apply to the filer.

Filings: whether the document is a withdrawal ('1'), a document that was withdrawn ('2'), or neither ('0'). Carried as published: a withdrawn filing is not dropped from the table, so that a population can be read as what was filed.

Filers: the day the filer's financial year ends, as the agency writes it ('5月31日' for 31 May), with no year in it and so not a date. Worth carrying because it says which filers do not close in March: of 3,816 listed filers in the list of November 2026, 1,633 do not.
Running number over the entity master data table, assigned in LEI order at each rebuild; dense but not stable across rebuilds.
For an investment fund on the ECB investment fund register, its investment policy as stated in the register (e.g. equity, bond or mixed fund).
For an investment fund on the ECB register, its fund type: ETF, PEF (private equity fund) or 'Neither ETF nor PEF' (renamed from 'Type of investment fund' and abbreviated).
For an investment fund on the ECB register, whether it is UCITS compliant: UCITS, or AIF for a non-UCITS alternative investment fund (renamed from 'UCITS compliance' and abbreviated).

Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442) of the entity, normalised the way GLEIF writes it (blanks removed, upper case); in the GLEIF Level 2 relationship data it is read from the start node of the relationship.

Sector of the entity, taken from the narrowest sectoral register it appears in: CCP (ESMA CCP list), INUN (EIOPA insurance undertaking), ORPI (EIOPA IORP), CB/CDTI/OFI/MMF or MFI (ECB MFI list, by category), or UCIT/AIFD/INVF (ECB investment fund register, by UCITS compliance).
Refinement of SECTOR offered by the register that set it: the type of CCP (EUCCP, T1CCP, T2CCP) for CCPs, or the investment policy for funds whose sector comes from the ECB fund register.
Filings: the time filings.xbrl.org added the filing to its repository (UTC).

Issues: the day the run that wrote the row was made. The issues of a partition are replaced as a whole when it is checked again, so this says when the rows that are there were found rather than when the problem arose.
Facts: the concept the fact reports, as a prefixed name of the taxonomy (e.g. ifrs-full:Revenue, ifrs-full:Equity, or an extension concept of the issuer).
Country the filing was collected from, as filings.xbrl.org codes it (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. AT, DE, GB); the partition column of the table of facts.
Facts: the decimals the issuer states for a numeric fact, i.e. to how many decimal places it is accurate (0 for whole units, -3 for thousands); empty for INF (exact) and for text facts.

Facts: the dimensions of the taxonomy the fact is reported for, as axis=member sorted and joined by ';' (e.g. ifrs-full:ComponentsOfEquityAxis=ifrs-full:RetainedEarningsMember); empty for a fact without dimensions, which is the total.
Filings: the number of errors filings.xbrl.org found when it validated the filing.
Facts: the identifier of the fact within its report, as the xBRL-JSON gives it; unique within a filing only.

Identifier of the filing at filings.xbrl.org: the LEI, the date, the filing system, the country and a number (e.g. 529900PD3SI453KAW989-2026-03-31-ESEF-AT-0); the name of its report in the Bronze layer.
Filings: the number of calculation inconsistencies filings.xbrl.org found in the filing.

Issues: the code of the data quality check the record failed, one row per check it failed. fincommons.dataquality.describe_check turns it into the sentence that says what the code means, how severe it is and what to do about it. A record nothing objected to has no row in the table at all.
Filings: address of the report as xBRL-JSON, relative to https://filings.xbrl.org; empty where the repository could not convert the filing, which then has no facts.
Language of the report (filings, read off the name of its file) or of a text fact (facts), as an ISO 639-1 code (e.g. de, en); empty where none is stated, as for the filings of the United Kingdom.
LEI of the issuer that made the filing; for a fact, read off its entity (scheme:LEI). The key that joins the filings with entitymasterdata.
Filings: the name of the issuer as filings.xbrl.org records it.
Filings: the SHA-256 of the report package as filed, as filings.xbrl.org gives it; what a collected package is checked against.
Filings: address of the report package as filed (.zip or .xbri), relative to https://filings.xbrl.org.
The last day of the period the filing reports on, usually the end of the financial year; on a fact, that of its filing.
Facts: the last day of the period of the fact, included, or the day of an instant; xBRL-JSON writes it as the start of the following day, which is converted back.
Facts: the first day of the period of a fact for a duration; empty for a fact for an instant, such as a balance.
Filings: the time filings.xbrl.org last processed the filing (UTC); a report is collected again where it changes.
Filings: the time the filing was published by its source, where the source states it; empty otherwise.
Filings: address of the report as XHTML with Inline XBRL, relative to https://filings.xbrl.org.
Filings: the filing system the filing was made under, read off FILING (ESEF, which the repository uses for the filings of the United Kingdom too, or UAIFRS).
Facts: the value of a fact without a unit, as text, and of a fact with a unit whose value is not a number; text blocks, which carry markup, are left out of the table.
Facts: the unit of a numeric fact (e.g. iso4217:EUR, xbrli:shares, iso4217:EUR/xbrli:shares, xbrli:pure); empty for a text fact.
Facts: the value of a numeric fact, as reported, in UNIT and without any scaling (a report in thousands tags the full amount); empty for a text fact.
Filings: address of the report in the Inline XBRL viewer of filings.xbrl.org, relative to https://filings.xbrl.org.
Filings: the number of warnings filings.xbrl.org raised when it validated the filing.
ISO 4217 code of the base currency of the rate: EUR for ECB and (converted) BIS rates, or the rebase currency where the table is rebased.
Helper column: the rate used to convert a series, i.e. the EUR to rebase-currency rate on the same date (renamed from VALUE), or in the BIS conversion the EUR/USD rate; dropped from the final table.
Helper column: whether the EUR to rebase-currency rate used for rebasing on that date was itself carried forward from an earlier day (renamed from IMPUTED); dropped from the final table.

True where the day carries the last available rate of the pair from an earlier day (e.g. weekends, TARGET closing days) rather than a rate quoted on that day; after rebasing, also true where the conversion rate was imputed.
ISO 4217 code of the quoted currency (for BIS data the first three characters of the currency field).
Reference date of the rate, one row per calendar day in the Silver table (from 'Date' in ECB data, 'TIME_PERIOD' in BIS data).
Source of the rate: ECB, BIS, or whatever the proprietary (internal) rate file states; where several sources quote a pair on a date, internal takes precedence over ECB and ECB over BIS.
Kind of rate: 'ref' for ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates, 'avg' for BIS daily average rates, or as stated in the internal file.
Exchange rate: units of QUOTE per one unit of BASE. BIS USD-based rates are converted to EUR-based ones by multiplying with EUR/USD, and a rebase divides by the EUR to rebase-currency rate.
Bronze: the day the file was collected from the French Data Library, i.e. the day its text last changed in the Bronze layer.

Name of the file of the French Data Library the row comes from, as the library's page links it without the _CSV.zip suffix (e.g. F-F_Research_Data_Factors, 6_Portfolios_2x3); the partition column of the Bronze and the Silver table.

Frequency of the row: D (daily), W (weekly), M (monthly) or A (annual), read off the length of the period key (YYYYMMDD, YYYYMM, YYYY); weekly files key their rows by the last day of the week and are told apart by their name.
Bronze: the time the server of the library states the file was last modified (HTTP Last-Modified, in UTC); empty where the server does not state it.
Bronze: one line of the file as published, without its line end: preamble, notes, titles, headers, data rows and the copyright line alike.
Bronze: the number of the line within the file, from 1, which puts the lines back in order.
Silver build, intermediate: the lines of the text of one file, in the order of the file, gathered from the Bronze rows so that one task parses one whole file; not kept in the Silver table.
Reference date of the value: the day given for daily and weekly rows (for weekly rows the last day of the week), the last day of the month for monthly rows and 31 December for annual rows.

The column of the table the value is in, as the file's header names it, trimmed (e.g. Mkt-RF, SMALL LoBM, NoDur); for breakpoints the counts as the header names them or N where it names none, followed by the percentiles P05 to P100.

Code of the kind of table within the file, mapped from its title (e.g. FACTORS, RET_VW, RET_EW, NFIRMS, AVG_SIZE, BEME_VW, BREAKPOINTS); a title no rule maps keeps a code made from the title. See famafrenchdata.parse.TABLE_CODES.
Title of the table as the file publishes it, whitespace collapsed (e.g. 'Average Value Weighted Returns -- Monthly'); empty for the untitled first table of a factor file and for breakpoints.

The value as published: returns and factors in percent, counts of firms, average size in millions of dollars, ratios as stated by the table; the missing values -99.99 and -999 are left out rather than written.
The central index key of the registrant, which a filing with the Commission states. Empty for an ESEF filing; see LEI.

The concept the fact was tagged with, as the prefix the filing bound and the element name. It is not resolved across frameworks: ifrs-full:Revenue and us-gaap:Revenues stand as they were filed, and what the two have in common is a judgement the mapping module records rather than a fact the table asserts.

The member state whose mechanism the report was filed with. Empty for a filing with the Commission, which is filed with no member state; the absence is what the regime states, not a value that is missing.

The dimensions the fact was reported under, as the ESEF table states them. Empty means the fact is for the entity as a whole, which is true of every row the Commission contributes, its company files carrying no breakdowns at all. What is missing on that side is therefore rows and not values; see coverage().
The fact within its filing. It identifies a fact together with FILING and not on its own.
How many facts of the filing the table holds. For an ESEF filing it is counted from the facts, the index saying nothing about it.

The filing the row belongs to, as its own regime identifies it: the identifier of the repository for an ESEF report, the accession number of the Commission for a filing with it. The two are not drawn from one series and are only unique within a source.
The form a filing with the Commission was made on, such as 10-K or 20-F. Empty for an ESEF filing: the regime has one kind of report and names no form.

The accounting framework the filing was prepared under, IFRS or US-GAAP, taken from the prefix the filing bound to the taxonomy it tagged against rather than from the regime it was filed under. A foreign private issuer reporting under IFRS to the Commission is therefore recorded as IFRS, which is what makes it comparable with the European reports.

The legal entity identifier of the issuer, which ESEF prescribes and which is the key of the entity master data as well. Empty for a filing with the Commission, which states a central index key instead; neither body publishes a mapping between the two, GLEIF's register pointer naming EDGAR for some tens of thousands of records that are nearly all funds, so neither column is derived from the other and exactly one of them is filled.
The measure a fact is taken to be, such as revenue, where with_measures has labelled it. Empty for the great majority of facts, which no measure names.
Which concept of a measure this is, lowest first, where a filing states several of them. The catalogue says why that order and what the caveat is.
The name of the issuer, as its own publisher holds it.
The last day of the period the filing reports on. The earlier periods a filing states are its comparatives.
The calendar year PERIODEND falls in. The table of facts is partitioned by it after SOURCE.
The last day of the period the fact is about, or for a fact reported at an instant, the day it stands for.
The first day of the period the fact is about. Empty for a fact reported at an instant, which is how the two are told apart.
Which module the row came from, esef or sec. It is the first partition column of the table of facts, so that a question scoped to one regime passes over the other.
The value of the fact where it is not numeric. Empty for every row the Commission contributes, and not because this module drops it: the company files carry no narrative facts at all.
The unit of the fact, such as EUR, USD or shares. Empty for a fact that is not numeric.
The value of the fact where it is numeric.

Action type: the delta-file element a record was reported in, NewRcrd (new), ModfdRcrd (modified), TermntdRcrd (terminated) or CancRcrd (cancelled); it determines how the record changes the instrument history.
Date and time the issuer approved the admission to trading or trading of its instrument on the venue (RTS 23 field 9, date of approval of the admission to trading).
Classification of the instrument as an ISO 10962 CFI code (RTS 23 field 3). In the compact table, the distinct codes reported by the venues for an ISIN joined with '+'.
Commodity derivative indicator: whether the instrument is a commodity derivative (RTS 23 field 4).
Reference date of the FIRDS file (Bronze partition) a record was read from, i.e. the publication date of the full or delta file.
Seniority of a debt instrument (RTS 23 field 23): SNDB senior, MZZD mezzanine, SBOD subordinated or JUND junior.
Delivery type of a derivative (RTS 23 field 34): PHYS physical, CASH cash or OPTL optional.
Date and time of admission to trading or of the first trade on the venue (RTS 23 field 11).
Full name of the financial instrument (RTS 23 field 2).
Identifier of the reference rate (index or benchmark) of a floating rate debt instrument: its ISIN, index code or name, according to INTRSTRATEFLTGIDTP (RTS 23 fields 19 and 20).
How the reference rate of a floating rate debt instrument is identified in INTRSTRATEFLTGID: ISIN, Index (index code) or Name; derived from which of the three elements is filled.
Spread in basis points over the reference rate of a floating rate debt instrument (RTS 23 field 22).
Unit of the term of the floating reference rate (RTS 23 field 21): DAYS, WEEK, MNTH or YEAR.
Number of units of the term of the floating reference rate (RTS 23 field 21), e.g. 3 for a three-month rate.
Fixed interest (coupon) rate of a debt instrument, in percent (RTS 23 field 18).
Instrument identification code: the ISIN of the financial instrument (RTS 23 field 1).
Whether the admission to trading or trading on the venue was requested or approved by the issuer (RTS 23 field 8).
LEI of the issuer, or of the trading venue operator where the instrument has no issuer (RTS 23 field 5). In the compact table, the distinct values across venues joined with '+'.

Whether the version is the most recent one received for its instrument, i.e. the LATESTRECORD flag of section 4.2 of ESMA65-8-5014. One version of an instrument carries it at a time, which is what the first query of section 4.3 selects on.
In the FIRDS watermark (metadata) table, the reference date of the newest file applied to the named table. The update applies every delta file newer than it and none that is older.
Maturity date of a debt instrument (RTS 23 field 15). In the compact table, the value the venues agree on, empty where they disagree.
In the FIRDS watermark (metadata) table, the table of the Silver layer the row records the watermark of, e.g. MAIN. The table holds one row per such table.
Nominal value per unit, or minimum traded value, of a debt instrument (RTS 23 field 17).
Currency of the nominal value per unit of a debt instrument (ISO 4217).
Notional currency of the instrument (RTS 23 field 13, notional currency 1), ISO 4217.

Tag naming what an incoming record does to the version in force, CLOSE_AND_INSERT or REPLACE. It is attached to the plan a delta file implies, which the merge of the Silver layer reads and no table stores.
Option exercise style (RTS 23 field 33): EURO, AMER, ASIA, BERM or OTHR.
Option type (RTS 23 field 30): CALL, PUTO or OTHR.
Price multiplier of a derivative: the number of units of the underlying represented by one contract (RTS 23 field 25). In the compact table, the value the venues agree on, empty where they disagree.
Date and time of the request for admission to trading on the venue (RTS 23 field 10).
Short name of the instrument, the ISO 18774 FISN (RTS 23 field 7). In the compact table, the distinct names across venues joined with '+'.

Technical attribute: start of the record's publication period in FIRDS, from whichever branch of the period is stated (FrDt, FrDtToDt.FrDt or Dt), falling back to the file's reference date for terminations and cancellations that state no period.
Technical attribute: end of the record's publication period in FIRDS, stated for records whose publication has ended (terminations).
Technical attribute: the relevant competent authority for the instrument, as a two-letter country code.
Technical attribute: MIC of the relevant trading venue, the most relevant market in terms of liquidity for the instrument.
Termination date: date and time the instrument ceases to be traded or admitted to trading on the venue (RTS 23 field 12).
Total issued nominal amount of a debt instrument (RTS 23 field 14).
Currency of the total issued nominal amount of a debt instrument (ISO 4217; RTS 23 field 16, currency of nominal value).
Trading venue: the MIC of the venue the instrument is admitted to or traded on (RTS 23 field 6). In the compact table, the distinct venues of an ISIN joined with '+'.
In the FIRDS watermark (metadata) table, the timestamp at which the newest file (MAXDATE) was last applied to the named table.
First day the version of the instrument is valid on, taken from the start of the publication period as section 4.2 of ESMA65-8-5014 prescribes.
Last day the version of the instrument is valid on, empty while the version is the one in force. A superseded version is closed on the day before the version that replaced it begins.
Expiry date of a derivative (RTS 23 field 24). In the compact table, the value the venues agree on, empty where they disagree.

Issues: the day the run that wrote the row was made. The issues of a partition are replaced as a whole when it is checked again, so this says when the rows that are there were found rather than when the problem arose.

The central index key of the registrant, padded to the ten digits the company files use. Neither the Commission nor GLEIF publishes a mapping from it to the legal entity identifier the ESEF and entity master data tables are keyed by; the LEI records that name EDGAR as their register are nearly all funds, by series identifier, and this module invents nothing.

The concept a fact was tagged with, as taxonomy and name, for instance us-gaap:Revenues. It is not resolved across frameworks: what a concept of one framework means in the other is a judgement, and not one this table makes.
The identifier of a fact. A company file gives its facts none, so one is made from what identifies a fact within its filing, which is what lets a file be read again without the table growing.
How many facts the filing stated, of the forms the run kept. It counts what the company file carries, which is the undimensioned numeric facts and not the whole of the filing.
The day the filing was made with the Commission.
The year of FILED, which the table of facts is partitioned by. The year a filing was made is monotonic; the fiscal year is not, since one filing states several of them.

The accession number of the filing the fact came from. A company file is organised by concept rather than by filing, so this is what a filing is reconstructed by, and a figure a later filing restates appears again under that filing rather than replacing the first.
The form the filing was made on, such as 10-K, 10-Q or 20-F. An amendment carries the form it amends with /A appended.
The fiscal period the filing reports on, as the Commission labels it: FY for an annual report, Q1 to Q4 for a quarterly one.
The Commission's own label for a period it considers comparable across companies, where it gave the fact one. It is carried as published and nothing here depends on it.

The accounting framework the filing was prepared under, IFRS or US-GAAP, taken from the taxonomies it tagged against. A foreign private issuer reporting under IFRS tags against the IFRS taxonomy and is recorded as such, rather than being taken for a US GAAP filer because of where it filed.
The fiscal year the filing reports on, as the Commission states it.

Issues: the code of the data quality check the record failed, one row per check it failed. fincommons.dataquality.describe_check turns it into the sentence that says what the code means, how severe it is and what to do about it. A record nothing objected to has no row in the table at all.
The name of the registrant, as the Commission holds it.

The last day of the latest period the filing reports on under a reporting taxonomy, which for a periodic report is the period it is about; the earlier periods in it are its comparatives. The cover page is not counted: it states a date after the period closed.
The last day of the period a fact is about, or for a fact reported at an instant, the day it stands for.
The first day of the period a fact is about. Empty for a fact reported at an instant, which is how the two are told apart.
The taxonomies the filing tagged against, separated by semicolons, for instance dei;us-gaap. FRAMEWORK is derived from them.
The unit of the fact, such as USD, shares or pure, as the company file names it.
The value of the fact. The company files carry the value and not the precision the filing claimed for it, which is why there is no decimals column.
